name: Jared Kushner
role: Senior Advisor to the President (2017–2021); US special envoy on Gaza, Ukraine and Iran talks (2025–); founder of Affinity Partners
summary: Kushner is a businessman-turned-negotiator who describes himself as a pragmatic, results-oriented dealmaker rather than an ideologue. His own record centres on a strongly pro-Israel Middle East strategy (the Abraham Accords, a 2020 peace plan favoring Israeli security claims), the bipartisan First Step Act on sentencing and prisons, USMCA and China tariffs, and a deregulatory, pro-market economic outlook. He says little on social issues such as abortion, marriage or guns.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Told a Harvard audience that capitalism is a very powerful force for improving lives, proven repeatedly, and credited deregulation and private-sector project management for results; he also praised state industrial planning in South Korea, so the view is pro-market but not absolute.

property-fundamental.rationale: Repeatedly argued that investment needs enforced property rights and that investors will not build where assets can be expropriated; his plan made private property protection a precondition for growth. He did not speak of overriding it in other contexts.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Praised the first-term deregulatory drive (cost of federal regulations fell four years running; more rules removed than added) and argued that new regulation tends to be captured by large firms, while granting that some regulation is needed.

strong-leader.rationale: Defended Congress and the founders' system against the claim that it is broken, but said hard problems in government need a 'courageous leader' and praised an outsider president who broke norms.

state-harmful.rationale: Said the founders were 'totally genius' in designing government, defended Congress as workable and urged business people to serve in government; his only criticism was that government has grown too big.

rehabilitation.rationale: Drove the First Step Act. Rejected the prison as a 'warehouse for human trash', argued prisons should offer job training and addiction treatment to cut re-offending and said he favored second chances, while acknowledging some offenders are dangerous.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Backed making the Fair Sentencing Act's reduced crack-cocaine penalties retroactive, describing the old 100-to-1 rule as racially disparate and 'racist'; this is one specific remedy, not a general programme.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His 2019 plan kept overall legal immigration levels static while shifting to merit and tightening the border; he also defended the lowest refugee admissions in 40 years.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Described the UN Security Council's treatment of Israel as anti-Semitic, halted US funding to UNRWA as corrupt, and said UN-linked aid had not delivered outcomes.

free-trade.rationale: Pushed USMCA as a 'win-win' record trade deal but also backed steel and China tariffs and said past trade deals 'should have been rebalanced'; he favors a level playing field with set rules rather than free trade as such.

nation-first.rationale: Described his foreign policy as pragmatic realism that pursues joint interests with other countries and builds trust; he also stressed protecting US economic interests against China and wanting an American-led order.

open-borders.rationale: Worked on and praised the roughly 470 miles of border barrier built in his term and urged leaders to secure the southern border and know who is in the country; he did not address eventual open borders.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Closed his Lex Fridman interview optimistic that AI, cheap energy and medical advances could deliver cures, abundance and a 'dawn for humanity', while saying human conflicts are separate man-versus-man problems.

experts-over-public.rationale: Repeatedly mocked Washington 'experts' (scare quotes) who fail for years and are still treated as authorities; commissioned focus groups of ordinary people and said the gap lies between experts and the public.

central-planning.rationale: Called capitalism a powerful, proven force for lifting living standards and built his Palestinian plan on private investment and property rights; praised Korean industrial planning only as one input.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Said the administration used a Section 232 national-security exemption to put tariffs on steel and aluminum 'to protect our steel industry', and defended China tariffs as slowing Chinese dominance.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Cited South Korea's 'strong industrial planning' as a success factor and favors national KPIs, but criticized Chinese state subsidies and said America's strength is its private sector.

military-superiority.rationale: Said peace comes 'through strength', that a very strong military exists chiefly to avoid war, and that he would prefer an American-led world order to a Chinese-led one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Described his approach as 'first principles, results oriented', said Trump is 'not terribly ideological' but 'about results', and contrasted outcome-driven business with process-driven diplomacy.

state-as-business.rationale: Argued government needs people with business mindsets, private-sector project management and published KPIs, as with his border-barrier work and Saudi Vision 2030; said nothing about citizens as customers.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said Jews have faced oppression and have a homeland to fight for; the plan he authored required Palestinians to recognize Israel as the Jewish state, and he backed US recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital.

national-self-determination.rationale: Called a Palestinian state a worthy goal if it cannot harm Israel and must be earned, said proactive recognition would reward terror, and left naming it to the Palestinians; his plan gave a limited-sovereignty state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Criticized the Biden administration for curbing domestic oil and shale production and pipelines, saying this raised prices and weakened US leverage.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said many Americans felt both parties' dynastic political class did not represent them, and called Washington a 'sick game'; he also defended politicians as 'gladiators'.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said everyone shares the same blood and wants a better life, urged never judging people by their worst mistake, and said Jews, Muslims and Christians are alike at heart.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Rejected framing Israel as an occupying power, stressing the 2005 Gaza withdrawal, the defensive 1967 war and deep Jewish ties to the land.

separated-powers.rationale: His plan made an independent judiciary and separation of powers conditions for Palestinian self-government, and he said a functioning judiciary is a prerequisite for a state.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Celebrated rebuilding trust with traditional allies, pressing NATO members to pay a fair share rather than leave, and building a Gulf-Israel security architecture.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Called Palestinian aid 'entitlement money' with no outcomes, cut UNRWA funding as a waste of taxpayer dollars and backed only conditions-based aid.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: His plan had Israel cede territory and swap land for a Palestinian state, and he got Israeli leaders to map it; he also called Israel's unilateral 2005 Gaza pullout a disaster and kept the Jordan Valley under Israel.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Urged recognition of Israel's annexation of the Golan Heights and of Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara as 'truths', and his plan placed the Jordan Valley under Israeli sovereignty.

character-from-environment.rationale: Said hatred is learned and that circumstances can push people to a worse place, but also that some people are simply evil.

refugee-return.rationale: The plan he led said there would be no right of return or absorption of any Palestinian refugee into Israel and limited refugee status; he called UNRWA's multi-generational refugee status a perpetuating device.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Told Lex Fridman that people should 'suit up and go play' rather than sit in the stands and that citizens with the chance to serve have agency and a responsibility to try to improve the world.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: His development plan relied on foreign private investment and Gulf funding, tied to property rights and rule of law, rather than on self-financing alone.

corporate-influence.rationale: Argued that big banks and other large institutions shaped post-crisis banking legislation to their benefit, entrenching regulatory capture; said nothing about lobbying or campaign money generally.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Told Harvard students capitalism is 'a very powerful force towards improving people's lives' that has been proven repeatedly, and built his Palestinian plan on private investment.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Argued the Haram al-Sharif is a Jewish holy site beneath a mosque and that Jews have an ancient homeland, yet repeatedly urged leaving old grievances and history behind to solve things pragmatically.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Speaks of the Holocaust as historical fact, including the Grand Mufti's link to Hitler 'once the Jewish people were annihilated' and his own grandparents as post-war refugees.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Praised Israel as a place where gay people can parade and live freely and condemned Hamas for killing gay people in Gaza; he did not address criminal law in general.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Faulted the Palestinian leadership for lacking democracy, free speech and a free press and praised Israeli open dissent as a sign of vibrant democracy.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Said Islam is at its core a peaceful religion, praised Saudi efforts to restore it as a religion of tolerance and rejected the idea that the West is at war with Muslims.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Said a very strong military is necessary for deterrence and urged strength toward Iran and Hamas.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Worked to reform prisons with job training and addiction programs, not abolish them; said some people are evil, cited police support for the First Step Act and wanted to keep the system.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Said Israel has the right to defend itself, called soldiers and civilians who risked their lives to free hostages heroes and backed removing Hamas militarily.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Credited secrecy and operating 'below the radar' for the Abraham Accords and peace plan, said nothing leaked from his team, and urged ignoring public statements in Middle East diplomacy.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Demanded that Hamas disarm and give up its weapons and tunnels, and said the plan has an international force and a local Palestinian police to hold security; this concerns militias, not private citizens.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Drove the First Step Act, which cut some mandatory minimums for repeat drug offenders and widened judicial discretion; he argued offenders deserve individual second chances.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The 2020 plan required Palestinians to drop their ICC and ICJ actions against Israel and the US. His own view on international courts was not found.

multipolar-world.rationale: Said he would still rather have an American-led world order than a Chinese-led one, while also describing a coming 'G2' world; he did not argue for several independent poles.

notes:
Positions come from his own interviews and the plan he led, not from Trump administration policy generally. His 2024 remarks suggesting Gaza civilians be moved out to the Negev or Egypt and Gaza's 'waterfront property' being valuable are recorded; they concern a war zone, not a minority inside a country, so they are not scored on any statement. Immigration (merit-based plan) and social issues have no first-person evidence in the sources opened.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Living person: only his own words or his record are used. Most of the 490 statements are null because I found no statement by him. The Breaking History memoir text was not available to me, so its contents are not used. The plan terms (Jewish state, annexation, ICC clause) are used only at low confidence as he presented them. Gaza remarks come from a secondary report of a 2024 talk. Remarks on Iran sanctions (2020) and Ukraine talks (2025-26) were found but are not used: they are not clearly his own positions on any statement.
